title: The Subjunctive Mood
objectives: Use subjunctive in purpose clauses (ἵνα, ὅπως)

vocabulary.definition: in order that, so that (+ subjunctive)

grammar.explanation: The Greek subjunctive is formed by lengthening the thematic vowel (ο → ω, ε → η). It expresses purpose, possibility, exhortation, or prohibition. In dependent clauses, it follows ἵνα, ὅπως, ἐάν, ὅταν, etc.

paradigms.name: Subjunctive Uses
rows: ἔρχομαι ἵνα ἴδω (I come to see)

rules: Subjunctive has ω/η vowel (vs indicative ο/ε)

exercises.question: Form the aorist subjunctive 3rd singular of γράφω
Translate: ἦλθεν ἵνα μαρτυρήσῃ περὶ τοῦ φωτός.
exercises.answer: He came in order that he might testify concerning the light.

readingPassage.greek: Ἵνα πάντες πιστεύσωσιν δι' αὐτοῦ. Ἐὰν εἴπωμεν ὅτι ἁμαρτίαν οὐκ ἔχομεν, ἑαυτοὺς πλανῶμεν. Ἴδωμεν τί γίνεται.
readingPassage.translation: So that all might believe through him. If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves. Let us see what happens.
